task_brief: This is day 4 of "Digital Citizenship, Privacy, and Kindness Online". That is unit 1 in grade 4. Today is a build and test about reporting unsafe or unkind content. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Create a digital-safety guide for a younger learner using fictional examples and no real credentials. Today helps by working on reporting unsafe or unkind content. Your unit also covers digital footprints, evaluating a website for trust, strong practice passphrases, and reporting unsafe or unkind content. Today adds real evidence toward your unit project.
primary_task: Build something that solves a real need in your unit "Digital Citizenship, Privacy, and Kindness Online". Build it around what today covers: reporting unsafe or unkind content. First write what it must do. Write it so you can check it later. Then build it. Test it three ways: a normal case, a tricky case, and one you think will break it. Write down what happened each time. Fix anything that failed. Test again. Turn in the thing you built, your test notes, and one idea you tried but did not use. Everything you need is printed in activity_setup. It has the exact case, what should happen, how to try it, checks, and a paper choice worth the same score. Do not wait for another handout or app. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about reporting unsafe or unkind content. It is part of "Digital Citizenship, Privacy, and Kindness Online". Later days in this unit cover other things, like digital footprints. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about reporting unsafe or unkind content; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 4, try the steps yourself before you ask for help. Give a reason in your own words for at least one choice. A labelled drawing or a spoken answer counts fully.

central_input.title: Inline fictional decision case for reporting unsafe or unkind content
central_input.purpose: Classify and revise this case without opening a site, contacting anyone, signing in, or using real personal information.
scenario: A fictional app called Pebble Planner asks for a display nickname, exact birth date, home address, and contact list before showing a simple homework timer.
Its notice says the nickname is needed to label the timer, but gives no reason for collecting an address or contacts.
A fictional message then pressures the learner to reveal a sign-in secret immediately or lose the timer.
decision_options: B: stop, share no information, save a description of the message, and ask a trusted adult
C: invent an address but reveal a sign-in secret

expected_behavior_and_specification: The response must apply reporting unsafe or unkind content to at least three labelled details from the supplied central input.
Every conclusion must identify the exact row, card, requirement, or scenario sentence that supports it.
The response must include one concrete revision or decision and explain the check that would show whether it worked.
The response must name one thing the supplied case does not tell you instead of guessing.

execution_method.primary: Paper-first method: copy the short labels, annotate them, and complete the response in a notebook or any notes app. No download, installation, account, or internet access is needed.

execution_method.check_path: Use the numbered specification and the package test/check criteria as a checklist; a parent or tutor can verify the cited labels without needing subject software.

one limitation, unknown, or trade-off stated without inventing facts

debugging_target.passing_change: The exact accepted evidence map is intentionally withheld from learner material and is available only in the restricted trusted-adult scoring authority after the learner submits complete evidence.

concept_teaching.title: Pause, minimize, verify, and document: reporting unsafe or unkind content
concept_teaching.entry_check: Before reading, write one prediction about reporting unsafe or unkind content and one observation that could show the prediction is wrong. This readiness record is no-penalty evidence.
explanation: reporting unsafe or unkind content is about making a clear choice and showing why it works. First name what the result should do. Then point to the step, label, or fact that supports your choice.
A check is different from a guess. Write what you expect before you try it. Compare what happened with what you expected. If they differ, circle the first place they stop matching.
A fix needs a reason. Change one thing that your evidence supports, try the same checks again, and keep the old and new work. That record shows your thinking even when the first try was wrong.

Separate the stated purpose from the information or action requested, choose the least-exposing safe response, and record which printed detail supports the decision. You may use paper, objects, labelled drawings, or precise steps when a computer is not the best tool.

key_terms.definition: Collecting or sharing only what a stated purpose actually needs.
Clear authorization for a specific action and scope.
Checking a claim through evidence independent of the claim itself.
Stopping and involving a trusted adult or responsible authority when risk exceeds the learner’s role.

worked_example.title: Worked analogue: minimize a fictional club timer
worked_example.complete_analogue_case: A paper-only club timer needs a made-up activity label and duration. Its draft form also asks for an exact birth date and contact list even though neither supports timing.

annotations.reasoning: State the purpose first: label and time a fictional activity.
Match each requested field to that purpose; the date and contacts have no supplied justification.
Choose the least-exposing response: omit unrelated fields and keep the case offline.
Check by confirming every retained field has a stated function.
Escalate rather than supplying information if a real tool demands unrelated data or sign-in.

worked_example.completed_model: State the purpose first: label and time a fictional activity. Match each requested field to that purpose; the date and contacts have no supplied justification. Choose the least-exposing response: omit unrelated fields and keep the case offline. Check by confirming every retained field has a stated function. Escalate rather than supplying information if a real tool demands unrelated data or sign-in.

debugging_reasoning.title: Use the six-move evidence cycle
required_moves: Symptom: record expected versus actual without explaining it away.
Hypothesis: state one falsifiable cause about the claim or design state before revising.
Inspection: identify the first trace row or printed detail that bears on the hypothesis.
Predicted effect: state what one controlled change should alter and what it should leave unchanged.
Test and interpretation: compare actual with the prediction and mark the hypothesis supported, rejected, or not fully tested.
Verification: rerun all relevant checks and record any new limitation or next hypothesis.
debugging_reasoning.anti_guessing_rule: A working final artifact without a pre-change hypothesis and inspectable evidence is incomplete debugging/revision evidence.

remediation_routes.learner_signal: My conclusion names the topic but does not connect to exact printed evidence.
remediation_routes.title: Different representation: evidence cards and arrows
remediation_routes.alternate_teaching: Copy each printed fact onto a separate card. Draw an arrow from a fact to a claim only when the fact would make that claim more or less credible. Unconnected claims must be revised or removed.

remediation_routes.learner_signal: I changed or chose something before recording the mismatch and a testable reason.
remediation_routes.title: Different routine: the six-box evidence ladder
remediation_routes.alternate_teaching: Use six boxes in order: expected/actual, first divergence or decisive detail, hypothesis, predicted effect, one revision, rerun interpretation. Do not enter the revision box until the first four constrain what the change is meant to test.
remediation_routes.analogue_task: Apply the six boxes to a separate fictional clock-card mismatch related to reporting unsafe or unkind content. Stop after the prediction, explain what result would reject the hypothesis, then finish the check.
remediation_routes.return_check: Complete the fresh mastery check independently. A correct but low-confidence response receives confirmation tied to evidence, not automatic reteaching.

test_or_check_criteria: You wrote what it must do before you started building.

Nothing uses a real password, a real account, or a real website.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You can do this with the keyboard only, no mouse needed. Text can be made bigger, and you may do it on paper instead of a screen.
This work takes more than one sitting. Ask for a simple checklist with dates so you know what to do next. Keeping track is not part of your grade.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never require a real password, private message, precise location, account credential, API key, or identifiable image.
Use only fictional or sandboxed systems, accounts, and data; never probe, exploit, or attempt to access a real external system.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify, not as an authority or a substitute for learner work.
The tutor may explain, demonstrate, or debug alongside the learner, but must not silently complete a graded project or assessment for them.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting reporting unsafe or unkind content.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for reporting unsafe or unkind content follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for reporting unsafe or unkind content, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for reporting unsafe or unkind content works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of reporting unsafe or unkind content, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking reporting unsafe or unkind content mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply reporting unsafe or unkind content under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on reporting unsafe or unkind content rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
